a clean pull completes normally without creating recovery records
a corrupt config is propagated instead of being interpreted as an unset upstream
a gone upstream still opens the existing complete setup choices without changing config
a linked worktree cannot use the main worktree recovery even on the same branch
a pull conflict can be rolled back after service recreation and stash reordering

aborting and restarting the same merge on the same branch invalidates old pull recovery
an actually missing upstream still receives the missing-branch explanation
an invalid repository is reported without opening pull setup
an old pull snapshot cannot reset or clean up another branch
fast-forward pull with a stash-apply conflict can return to the pre-pull head
pull preserves SSH authentication errors instead of reporting a missing branch
resolving a stash-apply conflict cleans up the bound snapshot without changing HEAD
resolving the original pull merge restores saved local changes and removes only its snapshot
the upstream probe follows the linked worktree rather than the main worktree branch
upstream probes always observe current configuration and preserve actual pull validation
